newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer in continued liquidity on Monday.
The central Reserve Bank sold Z$500 million worth of treasury bills at 15.93 percent to mop up the excess liquidity and dealers said other rates had also eased in sympathy.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 16.35 percent from 17 percent and sold at 16 percent from 16.75 percent while bankers acceptance bills slipped to 16 and 15.75 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 16.75 and 16.50 percent.
Call money eased to 15.50 from 15.75 percent in a market which opened in surplus of Z$122.1 million from a previous Z$257 million shortage.
